how: The proposal to surround the existing figure with hcjWows calls for further shared work rather than documenting the initial recruitment of its makers.
Praise and collective accomplishment do not establish recruitment unless a passage also calls for work or reports joining it.
A one-line maintenance commitment follows its author's own proposal, fitting bare commitment without demonstrating that another member joined.
The self-authored proposal and commitment cannot establish the mechanism of recruiting another member through a call and acceptance pair.
The opening claims collective accomplishment without showing who first proposed or placed the mark.
Participants claim the figure as shared work, recognise its community reference, and report adding the crab.
Repeated updates report the figure standing, the crab underway, and the yellow stains appearing.
A new-location link and a coordinate reply make the returned work findable without establishing a shared pixel template.
Volunteering to coordinate and reporting Discord planning establish neither appointed order nor its absence, and cannot test the aggregate frequency claim.
Participants promise maintenance and prioritise holding borders over changing the background.
The invasion reporter corrects the attributed attackers after noticing the writing, documenting revised attribution rather than independently verified responsibility.
Reported fatigue after returning the picture does not show that scripts, bots, or spare accounts were used.
The peace objection pushes back against a war proposal without establishing that the objection stopped any placements.
References to peace and maintaining borders do not disclose a neighbour's proposal, agreed terms, or bilateral negotiation.
A relocation proposal during reported invasion is followed by loss, return, and a new location, while the detailed move decision remains unavailable.
Needing sleep after recovery does not state that insufficient hands or room forced relocation.
The joke about borrowed portals reports help but cannot establish assistance exchanged between actual rooms.
Naming a planning Discord does not establish a coalition of rooms.
Maintaining borders does not show that the work lived under another room's territorial rule.
The returned account of planning names no member carrying a proposal between rooms.
War and peace are contrasting tactics here, without any expressed dispute over who may bind the room to an agreement.
Participants announce collective accomplishment and express recognition and pride in the makers.
A posterity picture, condition updates, mourning, survival report, and damage qualification preserve successive states during and after the work.
The splash qualification narrows reported survival without requesting cleanup, choosing between preserved versions, or disputing a historical account.
Saving a posterity picture and announcing survival do not show a decision to continue, repurpose, or remake the collective effort.
Familiar figures and sayings make the canvas work recognisable to participants without establishing shared understanding across all room members.
Attributing the covering to the Netherlands does not establish a quarrel predating the canvas.
The claim to making the figure does not establish an April Fools prank frame for the host room.
Using a thread and a planning chat does not establish moderator routing, a posting rule, or a decision containing canvas talk.
War rhetoric responding to a proposed background cannot distinguish defacing another work from defending the existing figure.
Participants carry the loss in talk through lament, blame, and jokes about the attributed attackers inside their own thread.
The named attackers are not linked to an earlier rivalry or tie that explains a call to attack.
The visible call follows an already claimed accomplishment, leaving the original recruitment-to-building mechanism untestable.
A collective accomplishment does not identify the starter or show how a starter prompted recruitment.
The same speaker shows the picture appearing and then commits to maintaining it, supporting a build-to-upkeep transition without identifying individual pixel actions.
Upkeep and border priorities are visible, but the planning account does not disclose a turn toward negotiating with neighbours.
The peace objection does not disclose settled border terms whose authority then produces restraint.
Loss and tired recovery do not reveal whether upkeep led to machine placement.
The return announcement receives explicit celebration of seeing the work again, supporting the transition to marking accomplishment.
The observed announcement-to-posterity sequence does not establish that collective celebration motivated preservation.
Recording and survival reports are not followed by a coded decision about what to carry into later collective activity.
A move is reported without a judgement that too few hands forced the room to abandon its spot.
A proposal and later coordinates do not disclose a design argument settled by a pixel template.
The portal-help joke cannot establish that strained upkeep produced a request for help from another room.
Neither the border account nor the portal joke discloses a negotiated channel subsequently used to trade help.
The maintenance proposal and later war rhetoric do not establish that recruited hands were turned against a rival's work.
The reasoned peace reply answers war rhetoric, but cannot establish restraint after an actual attack or an explicit call to deface another work.
Invoking peace does not disclose an attack followed by a neighbour's negotiation or a proposed bilateral deal.
Blame follows reported incoming covering, not an evidenced attack initiated by this room.
Maintaining borders while planning in a chat does not show that upkeep produced a coalition of rooms.
The visible work proposal supplies no evidence of a resulting post flood or host response containing canvas talk.
A peace objection and a border priority reveal neither an agreement's terms nor a subsequent dispute about whom it binds.
Maintenance includes planning in another venue and reporting a selected priority back to the thread.
The reported covering is answered by a return announcement and followed by a new-location report, without disclosing the causal move decision.
Recovery and relocation return the thread to locating and reporting the work, extending the model's move description without asserting a causal rebuilding loop.
Post-event incomprehension makes having been present a limit on understanding the shared achievement, which the standing processes do not explain.
Noticing another canvas picture remains a spectator action without requiring building, recruiting, or helping its makers.
